I have completed a systematic review of all 18 evidence candidates against their source excerpts. Here is the verdict summary:

---

## VERDICT SUMMARY

| evidence_id | chapter | Verdict | Primary Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| EF-Ea80ee23b17f8 | 5B.1/3/8 | **ACCEPT** | All 2022 tax percentages match excerpt (13.6% total, 7.9% income, 5.2% goods/services, 0.8% excises). |
| EF-E6bedbc02729f | 5B.1/3/6/8/9 | **ACCEPT** | All 2022 expenditure figures match (total 28.0%, subsidies 2.8%, fuel 0.5%, social benefits 4.1%, nonfinancial assets 2.3%). |
| EF-E282f97f9d631 | 5B.3/9/10 | **ACCEPT** | All fiscal/debt figures match excerpt (-3.8% overall balance, +0.7% primary, 56.2% gross debt, 48.5% net debt). |
| EF-Ed9521af43705 | 5B.4/9/10 | **ACCEPT** | All balance-of-payments dollar values match (CA -$17.3bn, trade -$27.4bn, exports $564.1bn, imports $591.5bn, remittances $55.1bn). |
| EF-E3a2e9f890ad7 | 5B.4/9/10 | **ACCEPT** | All GDP-ratio figures match (CA -1.2%, trade -1.9%, secondary income 3.8%, FDI -2.1%). |
| EF-Edcd97b974346 | 5B.3/4/10 | **ACCEPT** | All Q2 2022 banking indicators match (18.7% capital, 2.3% NPL, 143.4% provisions, 17.4% ROE, 38.5%/49.8% liquidity ratios). |
| EF-E03edd51ec428 | 5B.3/4/9/10 | **ACCEPT** | All June-2022 market indicators match (6.4% treasury rate, 380.9bps EMBIG, 8.4% 10yr yield, 10.7% credit growth, 2.3% NPL). |
| EF-E0906ac5da9a8 | 5B.3/9/10 | **ACCEPT** | All reserve/debt figures match ($203.6bn reserves, 3.9 months imports, 284.2%/123.3% adequacy ratios, 31.6%/20.6% external debt). |
| EF-E568804167ef3 | 5B.1/4/8/9/10 | **ACCEPT** | All 2022 growth and inflation figures match (GDP 2.1%, consumption 4.5pp, investment 1.0pp, net exports -1.0pp, end inflation 8.5%, avg 8.0%). |
| EF-Ef7f73014c0f6 | 5B.1/3/6/8/10 | **ACCEPT** | All 2022 public-sector figures match (-3.8%/0.7% balances, 21.0% investment, 2.8%/17.8% fixed investment, 19.8%/19.8% saving). |
| EF-Ef6e29bc8ead4 | 5B.3/4/10 | **ACCEPT** | Credit figures match (7.759 trillion pesos, 10.7% growth, 26.5% of GDP). Note: "expanded" in claim accurately reflects nominal increase. |
| EF-E35b75f71b346 | 5B.3/10 | **ACCEPT** | Annex I text directly states external position "broadly in line" with fundamentals, rebalancing attributed to reopening and fiscal gap, CA to stabilize near 1% medium-term. |
| EF-Ea637da3917ec | 5B.1/4/5/6/10 | **ACCEPT** | Annex I text confirms reforms were characterized as "critical to boost growth and exports in the medium and long terms" including informality, governance, energy, and Pemex. |
| EF-Ea9b09abcf40c | 5B.2/3/9 | **ACCEPT** | Direct excerpt confirms floating rate as shock absorber, intervention only for disorderly conditions, and Flexible Credit Line as buffer. |
| EF-Efc0a3d3fa863 | 5B.3/9/10 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms 23% gross public external debt, roughly one-quarter in local-currency bonds, NIIP sustainable, FX risks reduced, but large gross portfolio liabilities a vulnerability. |
| EF-Eb03834ff59b9 | 5B.1/3/8/9/10 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms CA deficit expected to widen to "around 1 percent of GDP," fuel price ceiling and subsidies "will weaken substitution and income effects" and "amplify their impact." |
| EF-Eee1d6f8889f9 | 5B.3/9/10 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms long maturity and local-currency reduce exposure, banking sector resilient, corporate hedges cover FX risk, but foreign-investor presence creates capital-flow reversal vulnerability. |
| EF-E558eb92c3a81 | 5B.2/3/9/10 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms free-floating commitment, no FX intervention in 2021, reserves $208bn (16% GDP), 131% ARA/254% short-term debt, reserves assessed adequate, Flexible Credit Line maintained. |
| EF-E2f95cfa05897 | 5B.3/9 | **ACCEPT** | Risk matrix excerpt shows commodity price shock likelihood = Medium, impact = Medium, with monetary policy response recommended "if shocks feed into core inflation." |
| EF-E6dae8a147825 | 5B.1/6/8/9 | **ACCEPT** | Risk matrix excerpt confirms social unrest Medium impact, with recommendations to tighten monetary policy, better-target social transfers, and accelerate low-income investment while avoiding fossil-fuel subsidies. |

---

**All 18 candidates are ACCEPTED.** Each excerpt directly and fully supports the corresponding claim's quantities, attributions, dates, and directional character. No factual distortions, invented data, or unsupported causal language were identified. Source limitations noted in each candidate's own record are accurate and appropriate.
